[page 1]
  Quasi-Static Magnetic Flux Tube Theory Note - Rev C

1. Flux-tube concept
A flux tube confines magnetic flux. Closed magnetic-field lines are represented by connected lumped magnetic
elements. At a magnetic node, signed fluxes satisfy continuity. In quasi-static models, field quantities are
complex phasors while a linear reluctance remains real.

2. Fundamental relations

Phi = integral_A B_n dA
Vm = integral_l H_n dl
Rm = Vm/Phi
For constant A and l: Rm = l/(mu0*mu_r*A)
B = Phi/A
H_iron = B/(mu0*mu_r)
H_air = B/mu0

3. Leakage split
The released leakage model is parameterized by sigma such that Phi_gap/Phi_core = 1-sigma and
Phi_leak/Phi_core = sigma. Because GAP-1 and LEAK-1 are in parallel, they have equal magnetic potential
difference.

R_leak = R_gap*(1-sigma)/sigma
R_parallel = 1/(1/R_gap + 1/R_leak)
Phi_core = N*I / (R_core + R_parallel)

4. Induced voltage
For a sinusoidal flux phasor at frequency f, induced-voltage magnitude is 2*pi*f*N*|Phi|. Orientation determines
the voltage sign/phase reference. The exciting and measuring coils are intentionally defined with opposite
induced-voltage orientation in the benchmark.

5. Explicit exclusions
Force interaction is excluded. The baseline benchmark does not use a nonlinear B-H curve, hysteresis,
eddy-current loss, or frequency-dependent permeability. A nonlinear inductor example may exist elsewhere but
it is not authority for this case.
